newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end mostly lower after bounce.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end mostly lower after bounce.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended mostly lower Thursday, except for gold, with the complex slipping back again after a two day recovery from the month long downtrend.
"Precious metals still look oversold and near long term support, with funds still short but commercials seeing value at these levels," Paine Webber analyst Bernard Savaiko said.

"There's been no significant bounce on the way down from the February highs, but we think some arbitrage desks are getting a little nervous about the low volatilities (implied in options prices) as a $10-15 bounce is not impossible."
COMEX December gold ended down 40 cents at $382.70 an ounce, after trading in a $381.00-382.80 range.
In bullion trade, spot gold ended quoted around $380.10, compared to the London Thursday afternoon fix at $378.85, and the New York close Wednesday around $379.70.
While sentiment remained bearish, analysts noted gold has bounced from the $370-380 level several times in the past three and a half years.
COMEX December silver ended down 2.2 cents at $4.905 an ounce, after trading in a $4.945-4.885 range.
The spot gold/silver ratio was little changed at 77.60 after declining in the past 10 days from an 18 month high of 78.55 on September 20.

The Philadelphia Stock Exchange's index of 11 precious metals stocks ended down 3.33 points at 116.90, and has fallen around 30 percent this year, a bigger fall than the nine percent fall seen in the spot gold price.
Gold saw an 18 month low at $376.90 this week, down from around $417 in February.

Investor demand for precious metals is seen limited by low inflation, and a strong equity market, while industrial and investor demand in other countries has been restrained by a strong U.S. dollar pushing up the cost of precious metals in local currencies, analysts said.
Technically, on the daily charts, momentum indicators have been showing some divergence from recent price downtrends, analysts noted.

But popular moving average indicators, such as the four, nine and 18 day triple moving-average trend following indicator, has not yet shown much sign of a turnaround for any of the four metals in the NYMEX/COMEX precious metals complex, analysts said.
NYMEX January 1997 platinum, now the active month with most open interest, ended down 30 cents an ounce at $388.00, while NYMEX December palladium closed down $1.15 at $121.10 an ounce.
-Clive McKeef, New York Commodities Desk, +1-212-859-1641 email: clive.mckeef@reuters.com
